# wordpress-performance-skills

> Open-source agent skills that audit and fix performance on **live production WordPress sites**,
> across whatever stack the site actually runs on. Point an AI coding agent at a WordPress URL and
> get a ranked, evidence-backed performance audit; give it more access and it can apply fixes with
> a rollback for every change. Licensed GPL-2.0-or-later. No telemetry.

**Status:** v0.1, usable but young. Both skills, a 20-entry defect catalog, the measurement
scripts and an evaluation harness are in place.

**Install:** `/plugin marketplace add billylui/wordpress-performance-skills` then
`/plugin install wordpress-performance@wordpress-performance-skills` in Claude Code, or
`npx skills add billylui/wordpress-performance-skills` for any agent supporting the Agent Skills
standard. Install `wp-perf-audit` alone for read-only measurement and reporting.

**The two skills:** `wp-perf-audit` measures and explains and changes nothing; `wp-perf-fix`
applies changes under a guarded write loop — one change at a time, each with explicit approval, a
rollback snapshot captured and verified first, a purge on the layer that actually holds the stale
copy, and verification of what a visitor really receives. A fail-closed validator refuses any
plan that violates those conditions.

## Is there a WordPress performance skill for AI agents?

Yes, several — and they cover different halves of the problem.

The official [WordPress/agent-skills](https://github.com/WordPress/agent-skills) collection
includes `wp-performance`, which is the right choice for **backend profiling of a local
checkout**: WP-CLI `doctor` and `profile`, database queries, autoloaded options, object caching,
cron, and remote HTTP calls. Its own frontmatter describes it as a "backend-only agent," and its
body states that it "assumes the agent cannot use a browser UI." It deliberately excludes frontend
Core Web Vitals.

**wordpress-performance-skills covers the half that one excludes**: the browser-visible, live-site,
builder-and-host-aware side. Core Web Vitals and their attribution, origin-versus-edge TTFB
separation, page-builder configuration defects that gate LCP, cache-layer diagnosis across CDN and
server and plugin and object caches, and a guarded write path for production.

They are complements. Install both.

## What makes this different from other WordPress agent skills

- **Works on a live site you operate**, not a repository checkout. Tier 0 needs only a public URL —
  no credentials, no plugin install, no setup.
- **Stack-general.** Elementor, Block Editor, Site Editor/FSE, Divi, WPBakery, Bricks, Beaver
  Builder, Oxygen, Breakdance, Brizy, and classic themes with no builder. PHP 7.4 and MySQL 5.7 are
  first-class targets, because a large share of real WordPress sites still run them.
- **Host-aware fixes.** Several managed hosts prohibit caching plugins and remove disallowed ones
  from the site. The fix path refuses changes the host forbids and routes to the permitted
  alternative.
- **Separates origin from edge.** A cached site's slow origin and its slow visitor experience are
  different problems with different fixes. A single blended number hides which one you have.
- **Finds configuration defects, not just heavy files.** The campaign this generalizes had its two
  largest wins in configuration: a 1.5 MB font that nothing referenced, and an entrance animation
  holding the LCP element invisible until JavaScript ran. Neither is visible to file-size analysis.
- **No vendor lock-in.** No proprietary MCP server or companion plugin required.
- **No telemetry, enforced in CI.** No analytics, no phone-home. The only network destinations are
  the site you name and hosts referenced by its own markup.

## Key documents

- [README](README.md): what it is, the cache-layer model, access tiers, and the audit/fix loop
- [docs/CONTRACTS.md](docs/CONTRACTS.md): JSON schemas and the invariants every script obeys
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): the no-egress guarantee and the safety model for production writes
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add support for a builder, host, or cache layer
- [evals/](evals/): scenarios, seeded-defect fixtures, and the no-skill baseline

## Core concepts

- **Access tiers** — 0 public (a URL alone), 1 admin (wp-admin/REST), 2 CLI (WP-CLI/SSH), 3 code
  (a deploy path). The audit works at whatever tier it has and states plainly what it could not
  check, rather than guessing.
- **Stack fingerprint** — builder, theme type, cache layers, CDN, host class, multilingual plugin,
  WooCommerce, and multisite are detected from public signals before anything else runs.
- **Evidence model** — every claim carries `{value, confidence, evidence[]}`. `unknown` is a
  first-class value. A confidently wrong claim about someone's production stack is worse than no
  claim at all.
- **Defect catalog** — universal defect classes organized by layer, with per-stack detection and
  fix sections inlined, so supporting a new builder or host is a new section rather than a rewrite.
